summary.intent: Coordinate the Callisto v1 alpha work as a lead session: launch and watch background sessions, track work packages and PRs, order merges, and later drive PRs #242/#246 (and #253) to zero review findings so the Codex reviewer finds nothing.
summary.outcome: Work package PRs were opened and tracked, #560 (A) merged and fixed the shared RUSTSEC-2026-0542 audit failure, and findings on #169/#173 were fixed and resolved. Later #634/#638 were pushed with findings resolved after adopting a local Codex review loop, #645 was moved to draft, and Codex-correction sessions were launched with #638 pushed Codex-clean. #242's corrections, the combined init integration pass and the #645 close were still pending.

repo: RUSTSEC-2026-0542 (humantime unmaintained via dev-dep trycmd) fails the cargo-deny audit on every PR; WP A owns deny.toml and carried the ignore, so all other PRs had to rebase after #560 merged.
Two PRs committed cargo-mutants output under mutants.out.old/ because .gitignore only covered mutants.out/; widened to mutants.out*/.
A plain git push can fail silently when the local branch name differs from its upstream; use an explicit refspec and verify with git ls-remote.
claude --resume needs the full session id, not the 8-character job id; the short id leaves the session stuck on a search screen.
Entire gates require reviewer approval and open findings must be resolved via `entire trail finding resolve`; each WP group maps to a semantic trail (#357, #457-#460).
Auto-mode classifier refused commits carrying a Claude-Session: trailer, which launch rules forbid; commits must be signed with no trailer.
Publish isolation (L) shares templates and init.rs with D (#565), and tokenless twine publishing (J, #569) must merge after L; merge chain is #565 -> L -> #569.
Codex CLI is installed locally; `codex review --base` cannot take a custom prompt, so the default review is used to mimic the PR reviewer.

code.finding: Windows $EDITOR splitter keeps backslashes and quoted whitespace; review found single-quoted Git-for-Windows paths regressed, fixed by honoring single quotes.
Real merge conflict between #563 (I) and #560 (A); #563 could not be auto-updated from main.

workflow: Run the same reviewer (Codex) locally on the whole PR in a loop until clean before pushing; Claude-agent reviews have different blind spots and kept leaving findings.
Patching low-severity findings one push at a time does not converge; fix the boundary/contract and adopt a stopping rule instead of spot fixes.
Verify subagent and peer claims against the remote (ls-remote, signature, diff) rather than trusting reports; one claimed push had not landed.
Prove regression tests fail without the fix; one new process-count test passed without the guard and so proved nothing.
Prototype risky designs as a spike against real tooling before opening a large PR (the Git boundary PR #645 parsed foreign output and was redesigned).
Do not tell the user all PRs will go green after a base merge without listing exceptions with real conflicts.

friction: Sandbox blocked the session daemon socket so agent commands had to be rerun outside it.
Session 2 sat on a worktree permission prompt only the user could answer, stalling D/J chain.
Session 3 and Session 5 exited with PRs still open; Session 5 resume failed by short id.
My status claim that #563 would go green after #560 merged was wrong due to the bench conflict.
Closing #645 was blocked by a permission check needing explicit user OK.
Edits to the codex-review script were blocked by a write-protected directory for shell commands.
Review rounds on #242/#246 kept yielding 3-5 new low findings per push and the user grew frustrated with the pace and with over-wordy prompt hints.
Flaky tests observed in full-workspace runs (registry_version_the_registry_serves_is_exact_with_no_checksum_or_yank_claim, init::tests::an_existing_config_errors).
Concurrent builds slowed the pre-push gate.
open_items: Close #645 (Git boundary) once the user says so; any non-GitHub tag push work should start as a real-Git spike.
#242 corrections (disabled inference bypass via is_active(), revert JSON field, prerelease batching) still need a Codex-clean pass before push.
Integration pass reconciling #242 and #246 conflicts in init.rs and verifying combined behavior.
Product-picker bare-alias UX decision for #246 and the changeset serialization round-trip fix.
Merge order remains: #562, #564, #561, #566, #565, #563, #567, #568, then L and #569; Session 4 (Q) launches after E and F2 merge; K waits on G.
Whether E's changeset is Breaking (recommended yes) was left undecided.
Unfixed lows tracked as follow-ups: remaining per-package git grep when manifest moved since pre.json.
Codex proposal to replace NAPI's three size models with core-owned footprints in the michi project was received but not acted on.
